subject: Request: 3-year uplift cap & renewal protection for Clearline - Exec signoff
messages:
From: Sam Ellison <sam.ellison@clearline.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@clearline.com>, Michael Chen <mchen@clearline.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 3-year commit pricing + renewal protection

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers look promising for the services we're planning. Our CFO wants a simple commercial ask before we move to legal: a 3-year committed pricing package with a firm uplift cap for each renewal year and a price-lock guarantee for the initial term.

Specifically, Clearline is requesting:
- Fixed unit price for the first 12 months (no mid-term increases)
- Uplift cap of 6% per year on renewals for years 2 and 3
- A renewal-protection clause: if Redwood introduces materially different pricing tiers, Clearline can opt to renew at the greater of (a) the capped uplift or (b) a one-time negotiated true-up with a maximum corridor of +10% for exceptional macro-driven increases.

I appreciate this is outside standard terms, but given the scale we expect in year 2 (forecasting ~5–6M annualized), this stability is a must for our board. Can you confirm Redwood is able to consider and, if so, what the commercial implications would be?

If helpful I can loop in our procurement lead.

Best,
Sam
Sam Ellison
Head of Procurement, Clearline Health

Attachments: None

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ellison <sam.ellison@clearline.com>, Priya Rao <priya@clearline.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 3-year commit pricing + renewal protection

Hi Sam — thanks for laying this out clearly. This is the right ask to bring forward. Per internal discussion with Deal Desk and Deal Economics, we can consider a bespoke 3-year package but it requires exec signoff because it changes our standard uplift guardrails and adds a renewal opt-out protection.

Proposal (internal recommendation):
- Term: 3 years, annual billing cycle
- Year 1 price: firm (no increases mid-term)
- Renewal uplift cap: 6% per year (years 2 & 3) — requested by Clearline
- Renewal-protection clause: Clearline may opt for a one-time true-up in the event of material public pricing changes, limited to a maximum corridor of +10% in any single year; any true-up must be mutually agreed and is only available at renewal window
- Discount / commercial concession: 28% volume-based average discount across the committed capacity (higher than standard for this cohort)

Impact & risks:
- Expected ARR ramp: Clearline expects ~5–6M by year 2 — we model net retention at ~1.12 under these terms
- Tradeoff: the renewal-protection clause widens our potential upside risk in inflationary scenarios and ties our hands for pricing evolution across similar customers without precedent

I've attached a short pricing summary and the revised SOW for legal review. Can I get executive approval to proceed with these exact guardrails (or guidance on any limits to uplift/discount) so we can draft the final term sheet and route to Legal/Procurement?

Attachments: Clearline_3yr_pricing_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet), Clearline_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW)

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: 3-year commit pricing + renewal protection — need exec decision

Jonas — forwarding the thread and attachments. Quick summary: Clearline (prospect moving to contract) is asking for a 3-year committed package with a 6% annual uplift cap and a renewal-protection/true-up mechanism capped at +10%. They also asked for a 28% blended discount on committed volumes.

Why this needs your attention:
- Discount: 28% exceeds our standard long-term discount guidance for this segment, requires approval beyond Deal Desk thresholds.
- Contract mechanics: the renewal-protection clause is a non-standard term that creates open exposure if we shift product pricing across the market. We should limit precedent or explicitly restrict to Clearline only.
- Financials: modeled cumulative revenue under these terms is attractive (projected 3-year revenue > 12M), but downside is potential compression if market prices rise.

Requested ask: Exec signoff to offer the proposed terms with the following guardrails (recommended):
1) Approve 3-year term and 28% blended discount as requested
2) Approve uplift cap at 6%/yr limited to years 2 & 3
3) Approve renewal-protection clause only if it includes an explicit carve (Clearline-only, non-transferable precedence) and a mutual review clause with Legal; any true-up process must require written business justification and CFO sign-off from Clearline
4) Limit overall concession allowance: if legal or procurement insists on additional concessions, return to Deal Desk for re-approval

Attaching the pricing summary and SOW again. If you approve, I will instruct Legal to prepare the term sheet and we will issue a conditional DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: 3-year commit pricing + renewal protection — need exec decision

All — reviewed the ask and the financial model. Approve proceeding with a conditional offer to Clearline under the following controls: 

1) Approve the 3-year term and the 28% blended discount as requested.
2) Approve the uplift cap at 6% per year for years 2 and 3, provided Legal adds explicit language that the uplift cap applies only to unit price changes at renewal and does not constrain other product fees (e.g., premium features) unless explicitly listed.
3) Approve renewal-protection with the following constraints: the clause will be Clearline-specific (no public precedent), any true-up requires: (a) written business justification from Clearline; (b) CFO-level sign-off on their side; (c) joint executive review if a proposed true-up exceeds 7% in a single year.
4) Require Legal to include a non-precedent footnote and a sunset review (internal) after 18 months to evaluate whether this creates adverse precedent risk.

Next steps:
- Marissa: instruct Legal to draft the term sheet with the items above and mark the HubSpot deal as "Exec-approved — legal drafting".
- Kimberly/Aditya: present the conditional term sheet to Clearline and confirm procurement timeline.
- Finance: we will coordinate to ensure revenue recognition treatment is reviewed once the SOW finalizes.

If Legal flags any material risk beyond the constraints above, escalate back to me before signing.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
